source.text: וַיְהִ֗י אַחֲרֵי֙ מ֣וֹת יְהוֹשֻׁ֔עַ וַֽיִּשְׁאֲלוּ֙ בְּנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בַּיהוָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר מִ֣י יַעֲלֶה־לָּ֧נוּ אֶל־הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֛י בַּתְּחִלָּ֖ה לְהִלָּ֥חֶם בּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And it was after [the] death of Joshua, and asked [the] sons of Israel of Yahweh, saying, Who will go up for us against the Canaanite[s] at the first, to fight against him?

en.L: And it was after the death of Joshua, and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, saying, "Who will go up for us against the Canaanites first, to fight against them?"
en.B: After Joshua died, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, "Which of us should go up first to fight against the Canaanites?"
en.R: After Joshua died, the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} asked {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} for guidance. "Which tribe should go first to attack the Canaanites?" they asked.

sw.L: Ikawa baada ya kifo cha Yoshua, wana wa Israeli wakamwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, wakisema, "Ni nani atakayetupandia kwanza dhidi ya Wakanaani, ili kupigana nao?"
sw.B: Baada ya Yoshua kufa, Waisraeli walimwuliza {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}}, "Ni nani kati yetu atakayepanda kwanza kupigana na Wakanaani?"
sw.R: Yoshua alipokwisha kufa, Waisraeli walimwomba {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} awaongoze. Wakamwuliza, "Ni kabila gani litangulie kwenda kuwashambulia Wakanaani?"

es.L: Y sucedió después de la muerte de Josué, que los hijos de Israel consultaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}, diciendo: «¿Quién subirá por nosotros contra los cananeos primero, para pelear contra ellos?»
es.B: Después de la muerte de Josué, los israelitas consultaron {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}: «¿Quién de nosotros debe subir primero a pelear contra los cananeos?»
es.R: Después de que murió Josué, los israelitas le pidieron dirección {{divine_name:al SEÑOR|a Yahvé}}. «¿Qué tribu debe ir primero a atacar a los cananeos?», le preguntaron.

fr.L: Et il arriva, après la mort de Josué, [que] les {{gender:enfants|fils}} d’Israël interrogèrent {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}}, en disant : « Qui montera pour nous contre les Cananéens en premier, pour combattre contre eux ? »
fr.B: Après la mort de Josué, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} demandèrent {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} : « Lequel d’entre nous doit monter le premier combattre les Cananéens ? »
fr.R: Après la mort de Josué, les {{gender:Israélites|fils d’Israël}} ont demandé {{divine_name:au SEIGNEUR|à Yahvé}} de les guider. Ils lui ont demandé : « Quelle tribu doit partir la première pour attaquer les Cananéens ? »

vi.L: Và xảy ra sau khi Giô-suê chết, con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} rằng: "Ai sẽ đi lên trước tiên cho chúng con để đánh người Ca-na-an?"
vi.B: Sau khi Giô-suê qua đời, dân Y-sơ-ra-ên cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}}: "Ai trong chúng con phải đi lên trước để đánh người Ca-na-an?"
vi.R: Sau khi Giô-suê qua đời, dân Y-sơ-ra-ên cầu hỏi {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} để biết phải làm gì. Họ hỏi: "Chi tộc nào phải đi trước để tấn công người Ca-na-an?"

ko.L: 그리고 여호수아가 죽은 뒤에 이스라엘 자손이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈어 말했다. "누가 우리를 위하여 먼저 가나안 사람들에게로 올라가서 그들과 싸우겠습니까?"
ko.B: 여호수아가 죽은 뒤에 이스라엘 백성이 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 여쭈었다. "우리 가운데 누가 먼저 올라가서 가나안 사람들과 싸워야 합니까?"
ko.R: 여호수아가 죽은 뒤에 이스라엘 백성은 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께 어떻게 해야 할지 여쭈었다. "어느 지파가 먼저 가서 가나안 사람들을 쳐야 합니까?"

pt.L: E aconteceu, depois da morte de Josué, que os filhos de Israel consultaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}, dizendo: "Quem subirá por nós primeiro contra os cananeus, para lutar contra eles?"
pt.B: Depois que Josué morreu, os israelitas consultaram {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}}: "Qual de nós deve subir primeiro para lutar contra os cananeus?"
pt.R: Depois que Josué morreu, os israelitas pediram {{divine_name:ao SENHOR|a Javé}} que os orientasse. "Qual tribo deve ir primeiro atacar os cananeus?", eles perguntaram.

decisions.choice: after the death of Joshua: the book begins where the book of Joshua ends
decisions.reason: Joshua's death and burial are told in Joshua 24:29-31. The book of Joshua opened with the same kind of words, "after the death of Moses" (Joshua 1:1), and Judges now opens the next stage in the same way: the tribes must go on without the leader who brought them into the land. Judges 2:6-10 steps back and tells Joshua's death again, to begin the account of the generations that followed. Some events in this chapter are also told in Joshua (the taking of Hebron and Debir, Joshua 15:13-19), so the chapter may gather the tribes' campaigns as a summary rather than keep strict order of time.

decisions.choice: asked of the LORD: sought God's answer, probably through the priest
decisions.reason: To "ask of the LORD" is to seek a decision from God. In Israel this was done through the priest, who carried the Urim and Thummim for this purpose (Numbers 27:21). The same question is asked in 20:18, at the other end of the book, where the tribes fight one of their own.

decisions.choice: the Canaanites: the peoples of the land as a whole
decisions.reason: "The Canaanite" is singular in the Hebrew, a name for the people of the land taken together, as in verses 3 and 4 where it stands beside other peoples. Here it means all who still held the land Israel was to take.

decisions.choice: who will go up for us first: which tribe is to lead the attack
decisions.reason: The question is not who should fight but who should begin, leading the rest. The answer in verse 2 names one tribe, Judah.

decisions.choice: for guidance; Which tribe
decisions.reason: Readable says what asking the LORD meant (m2) and makes plain that the question is about which tribe should lead, since the answer is a tribe (verse 2).

decisions.choice: the divine name as "el SEÑOR" in capitals by default ("El SEÑOR" at a sentence start, "del SEÑOR", "al SEÑOR"), with "Yahvé" under the divine name setting
decisions.reason: For the whole of Judges, as in the Pentateuch: the divine name is written "el SEÑOR" in capitals, like the English "the LORD", and the divine name setting gives "Yahvé". The span takes in the article and its contraction ("del", "al"), since "Yahvé" takes no article. "Jehová", the Reina-Valera form, is the alternative a Spanish reviewer may prefer.

decisions.choice: "los hijos de Israel" (L); "los israelitas" (B, R), with no gender span
decisions.reason: For the whole of Judges, as in the Pentateuch: Spanish "hijos" already takes in daughters, so the Literal "los hijos de Israel" (and "los hijos de Judá", "de Benjamín", "de Dan") is inclusive as it stands and needs no setting; Balanced and Readable say "los israelitas" or "la gente de", as the English does.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple at Literal and Balanced ("interrogèrent", "demandèrent") and the passé composé at Readable ("ont demandé"); speech in the tenses of speech at every level
decisions.reason: For the whole of Judges 1-10, as the French style guide and the terms note for Joshua, Judges and Ruth set for narrative: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative in French and suits a careful public reading, while the passé composé is how French is spoken and read in school today, so Readable uses it. What characters say keeps the tenses of speech ("je vous ai fait monter d'Égypte", 2:1).

decisions.choice: "le SEIGNEUR" for YHWH, with "Yahvé" as the reader setting; the span takes in the article and its contraction
decisions.reason: For the whole of Judges 1-10, as in the Pentateuch: the divine name is "le SEIGNEUR" in capitals by default, like the English "the LORD", with "Yahvé" as the reader setting ("du SEIGNEUR" / "de Yahvé", "au SEIGNEUR" / "à Yahvé"). "L'Éternel", the name used in the Segond tradition, is the alternative a reviewer may prefer; plain "le Seigneur" would hide that the name is used.

decisions.choice: "이스라엘 자손" (L) and "이스라엘 백성" (B, R) for "the sons of Israel", with no gender setting
alternatives: "이스라엘의 아들들" with a gender setting, as the English has
decisions.reason: The Korean words already mean the whole people, men and women, as in Genesis, so there are not two ways of saying it for a setting to choose between. The people ask God in the formal polite style (합쇼체), as in prayer. This holds for the whole block.

decisions.choice: "con cháu Y-sơ-ra-ên" (L); "dân Y-sơ-ra-ên" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "con cháu" (descendants) already includes men and women, so Vietnamese needs no gender setting here, and it is the Literal form of the Pentateuch; Balanced and Readable say "the people of Israel", as the English says "the Israelites".

decisions.choice: Israel prays to the LORD as "chúng con" (we, as children)
decisions.reason: People speaking to God use "con" for themselves, as in Genesis and Psalms.

decisions.choice: os filhos de Israel (L), os israelitas (B, R), with no gender setting
alternatives: os filhos e as filhas de Israel
decisions.reason: For the whole book, as docs/pentateuch-portuguese-terms.md and Joshua 1:2 set it in Portuguese: "filhos" already takes in daughters, and "os israelitas" names the whole people, so there is no second wording for the gender setting to offer. The same for "os filhos de Judá", "de Benjamim", "de Dã" (L) and "o povo de ..." or "os homens de ..." (B, R), as the English says.

decisions.choice: consultaram o SENHOR (L, B); pediram ao SENHOR que os orientasse (R)
decisions.reason: For the whole book (also 20:18, 23, 27): to ask of the LORD is to seek his decision (m2), and "consultar" says that in Portuguese, where "perguntaram ao SENHOR" would sound like an ordinary question. Readable says what the asking was for, as the English adds "for guidance".

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוָ֖ה יְהוּדָ֣ה יַעֲלֶ֑ה הִנֵּ֛ה נָתַ֥תִּי אֶת־הָאָ֖רֶץ בְּיָדֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Yahweh, Judah will go up; see, I have given the land into his hand.

en.L: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} said, "Judah will go up. See, I have given the land into his hand."
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "Judah is to go up. I have handed the land over to them."
en.R: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} answered, "The tribe of Judah will go. I have already handed the land over to them."

sw.L: Naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akasema, "Yuda atapanda. Tazama, nimeitia nchi mkononi mwake."
sw.B: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alijibu, "Yuda ndiye atakayepanda. Nimeitia nchi hii mikononi mwao."
sw.R: {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} alijibu, "Kabila la Yuda ndilo litakalokwenda. Tayari nimeitia nchi hiyo mikononi mwao."

es.L: Y dijo {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}}: «Judá subirá. Mira, he entregado la tierra en su mano.»
es.B: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} respondió: «Judá debe subir. Ya les he entregado la tierra.»
es.R: {{divine_name:El SEÑOR|Yahvé}} respondió: «Irá la tribu de Judá. Ya les he entregado la tierra.»

fr.L: Et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} dit : « Juda montera. Voici, j’ai donné le pays dans sa main. »
fr.B: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} répondit : « C’est Juda qui doit monter. Je lui ai livré le pays. »
fr.R: {{divine_name:Le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} a répondu : « C’est la tribu de Juda qui partira. Je lui ai déjà livré le pays. »

vi.L: Và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phán: "Giu-đa sẽ đi lên. Này, Ta đã phó xứ vào tay nó."
vi.B: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp: "Giu-đa phải đi lên. Ta đã giao xứ ấy cho họ."
vi.R: {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} đáp: "Chi tộc Giu-đa sẽ đi. Ta đã giao xứ ấy cho họ rồi."

ko.L: 그러자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 말씀하셨다. "유다가 올라갈 것이다. 보아라, 내가 그 땅을 그의 손에 주었다."
ko.B: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 대답하셨다. "유다가 올라가거라. 내가 그 땅을 그들에게 넘겨주었다."
ko.R: {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 대답하셨다. "유다 지파가 가거라. 내가 이미 그 땅을 그들에게 넘겨주었다."

pt.L: E {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} disse: "Judá subirá. Eis que entreguei a terra na sua mão."
pt.B: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} respondeu: "Judá é quem deve subir. Eu entreguei a terra nas mãos deles."
pt.R: {{divine_name:O SENHOR|Javé}} respondeu: "A tribo de Judá vai primeiro. Eu já entreguei a terra a eles."

decisions.choice: I have given: a promise spoken as already done
decisions.reason: The verb is in the form for a completed act. Before the battle is fought God speaks of the victory as settled, as he did to Joshua at Jericho (Joshua 6:2).

decisions.choice: given into his hand: placed under his power
decisions.reason: To give something "into the hand" of someone is to put it in their control. Judah is spoken of as one person, the tribe named after Jacob's son.

decisions.choice: handed the land over to them
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "them" for the tribe, where the Hebrew says "his hand"; Literal keeps the singular.

decisions.choice: God speaks in the plain style (해라체) with "나"
decisions.reason: As the terms of this translation set for God speaking to people, in Genesis and here.

decisions.choice: "phó ... vào tay" (L); "giao ... cho" (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps the Hebrew picture of the hand; Balanced and Readable say plainly that the land is handed over (m2). The same wording is kept wherever the LORD gives an enemy "into the hand" of Israel in these chapters.

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר יְהוּדָה֩ לְשִׁמְע֨וֹן אָחִ֜יו עֲלֵ֧ה אִתִּ֣י בְגוֹרָלִ֗י וְנִֽלָּחֲמָה֙ בַּֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י וְהָלַכְתִּ֧י גַם־אֲנִ֛י אִתְּךָ֖ בְּגוֹרָלֶ֑ךָ וַיֵּ֥לֶךְ אִתּ֖וֹ שִׁמְעֽוֹן׃

records.literal_gloss: And said Judah to Simeon his brother, Come up with me into my lot, and let us fight against the Canaanite[s], and will go also I with you into your lot. And went with him Simeon.

en.L: And Judah said to Simeon his brother, "Come up with me into my lot, and let us fight against the Canaanites; and I also will go with you into your lot." And Simeon went with him.
en.B: Judah said to his brother Simeon, "Come up with me into the territory allotted to me, and let us fight the Canaanites together. Then I will go with you into your territory." So Simeon went with them.
en.R: The people of Judah said to the people of Simeon, their relatives, "Come with us into the land given to us, and help us fight the Canaanites. Then we will go with you into your land." So the men of Simeon went with Judah.

sw.L: Naye Yuda akamwambia Simeoni ndugu yake, "Panda pamoja nami katika kura yangu, tupigane na Wakanaani; nami pia nitakwenda pamoja nawe katika kura yako." Naye Simeoni akaenda pamoja naye.
sw.B: Yuda alimwambia Simeoni ndugu yake, "Panda pamoja nami katika eneo nililopewa kwa kura, tupigane na Wakanaani pamoja. Kisha mimi nitakwenda pamoja nawe katika eneo lako." Basi Simeoni akaenda pamoja nao.
sw.R: Watu wa Yuda waliwaambia watu wa Simeoni, ndugu zao, "Njooni pamoja nasi katika nchi tuliyopewa, mtusaidie kupigana na Wakanaani. Kisha sisi tutakwenda pamoja nanyi katika nchi yenu." Basi watu wa Simeoni wakaenda pamoja na Yuda.

es.L: Y dijo Judá a Simeón su hermano: «Sube conmigo a mi suerte, y peleemos contra los cananeos; y también yo iré contigo a tu suerte.» Y Simeón fue con él.
es.B: Judá le dijo a su hermano Simeón: «Sube conmigo al territorio que me tocó en suerte, y peleemos juntos contra los cananeos. Después yo iré contigo a tu territorio.» Y Simeón fue con ellos.
es.R: La gente de Judá les dijo a sus parientes, la gente de Simeón: «{{plural_you:Vengan|Venid}} con nosotros a la tierra que nos dieron y {{plural_you:ayúdennos|ayudadnos}} a pelear contra los cananeos. Después nosotros iremos con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} a {{plural_you:su|vuestra}} tierra.» Así que los hombres de Simeón fueron con Judá.

fr.L: Et Juda dit à Siméon son frère : « Monte avec moi dans mon lot, et combattons contre les Cananéens ; et moi aussi j’irai avec toi dans ton lot. » Et Siméon alla avec lui.
fr.B: Juda dit à son frère Siméon : « Monte avec moi dans le territoire que le sort m’a donné, et combattons ensemble les Cananéens. Ensuite j’irai avec toi dans ton territoire. » Et Siméon partit avec lui.
fr.R: Les hommes de Juda ont dit à ceux de Siméon, leurs frères de sang : « Venez avec nous dans le pays qui nous a été donné, et aidez-nous à combattre les Cananéens. Ensuite nous irons avec vous dans votre pays. » Alors les hommes de Siméon sont partis avec ceux de Juda.

vi.L: Và Giu-đa nói với Si-mê-ôn, anh mình: "Hãy cùng em đi lên phần đất bắt thăm của em, và chúng ta hãy đánh người Ca-na-an; rồi em cũng sẽ đi với anh vào phần đất bắt thăm của anh." Và Si-mê-ôn đi với nó.
vi.B: Giu-đa nói với Si-mê-ôn, anh mình: "Anh hãy cùng em lên vùng đất đã bắt thăm chia cho em, và chúng ta cùng đánh người Ca-na-an. Rồi em cũng sẽ đi với anh vào vùng đất của anh." Vậy Si-mê-ôn đi với họ.
vi.R: Người Giu-đa nói với người Si-mê-ôn, là bà con của họ: "Hãy đi với chúng tôi vào vùng đất đã chia cho chúng tôi, và giúp chúng tôi đánh người Ca-na-an. Rồi chúng tôi cũng sẽ đi với anh em vào vùng đất của anh em." Vậy người Si-mê-ôn đi với người Giu-đa.

ko.L: 그리고 유다가 그의 형제 시므온에게 말했다. "나와 함께 내 제비 [뽑은 땅]으로 올라가서 가나안 사람들과 싸우자. 그러면 나도 너와 함께 네 제비 [뽑은 땅]으로 가겠다." 그래서 시므온이 그와 함께 갔다.
ko.B: 유다가 자기 형제 시므온에게 말했다. "나와 함께 내게 제비 뽑아 나누어 준 땅으로 올라가서 같이 가나안 사람들과 싸우자. 그러면 나도 너와 함께 네 땅으로 가겠다." 그래서 시므온이 그들과 함께 갔다.
ko.R: 유다 지파 사람들이 친척인 시므온 지파 사람들에게 말했다. "우리와 함께 우리가 받은 땅으로 가서 가나안 사람들과 싸우는 것을 도와 다오. 그러면 우리도 너희와 함께 너희 땅으로 가겠다." 그래서 시므온 사람들이 유다와 함께 갔다.

pt.L: E Judá disse a Simeão, seu irmão: "Suba comigo ao meu lote, e lutemos contra os cananeus; e também eu irei com você ao seu lote." E Simeão foi com ele.
pt.B: Judá disse ao seu irmão Simeão: "Suba comigo ao território que me coube por sorteio, e vamos lutar juntos contra os cananeus. Depois eu também irei com você ao seu território." Então Simeão foi com Judá.
pt.R: O povo de Judá disse ao povo de Simeão, seus parentes: "Venham conosco à terra que recebemos e nos ajudem a lutar contra os cananeus. Depois nós iremos com vocês à terra de vocês." Então os homens de Simeão foram com Judá.

decisions.choice: Judah and Simeon: brother tribes whose lands were joined
decisions.reason: Judah and Simeon were both sons of Jacob and Leah (Genesis 29:33-35), and the tribe of Simeon received its towns inside the land of Judah (Joshua 19:1, 9). The tribes speak as the brothers they are named after.

decisions.choice: lot: the territory given by lot
decisions.reason: The land was shared out by casting lots before the LORD (Joshua 14:2; 18:10), so a tribe's "lot" is the land it received that way.

decisions.choice: territory allotted to me (B); the land given to us; the people of Judah, of Simeon (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "lot" means once and then says "territory". Readable speaks of the tribes as peoples rather than as two brothers, so that a young reader does not picture two men. Balanced and Readable say "them" and "Judah" where the Hebrew says "him".

decisions.choice: "kura" (L) and "eneo nililopewa kwa kura" (B) for the allotted territory
decisions.reason: Swahili "kura" is the lot that was cast, and by extension the share it gave, as the terms note sets for these books. Literal keeps the bare word; Balanced says that the land was given by lot, as the English Balanced says "territory allotted to me".

decisions.choice: "suerte" (L); "el territorio que me tocó en suerte" (B); "la tierra que nos dieron" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the lot by which land was shared out, and so the land itself (m2). The terms note for these books uses "suerte" for the lot; Literal keeps it as the land's name, Balanced says the land that fell by lot, and Readable says only the land given.

decisions.choice: "lot" (L); "le territoire que le sort m'a donné" (B); "le pays qui nous a été donné" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the piece of land each tribe received by lot (Joshua 14-19). French "lot" keeps the word at Literal; Balanced says how the land was given, and Readable, which speaks of the tribes as groups of people, simply says the land given to them, as the English does.

decisions.choice: Judah calls Simeon "anh" and himself "em"
decisions.reason: Vietnamese must say which brother is older. Simeon was Jacob's second son and Judah his fourth (Genesis 29:33-35), so the tribe of Judah speaks as the younger brother; Readable, which speaks of the two peoples (m1), uses "chúng tôi" and "anh em".

decisions.choice: "phần đất bắt thăm" (L); "vùng đất đã bắt thăm chia cho" (B); "vùng đất đã chia cho" (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word is the lot by which the land was shared out (m2); "thăm" is the word for the lot in these books.

decisions.choice: Judah and Simeon speak to each other in the plain style between equals (해라체), as brothers
decisions.reason: The two tribes are spoken of as brothers; Korean uses the plain style between equals. "제비" (lot) is kept at Literal, with the land it gave in brackets.

decisions.choice: o meu lote (L); o território que me coube por sorteio (B); a terra que recebemos (R); você (L, B), vocês (R)
decisions.reason: "Lote" is both a share drawn by lot and a plot of land in Brazilian Portuguese, so Literal keeps the Hebrew picture (m2) in one ordinary word; "sorte" would read as luck. Balanced says once how the land was shared, as Joshua 14:2 has it in Portuguese ("por sorteio"). The brothers speak to each other with "você"; Readable, which speaks of two peoples, says "vocês".

source.text: וַיַּ֣עַל יְהוּדָ֔ה וַיִּתֵּ֧ן יְהוָ֛ה אֶת־הַכְּנַעֲנִ֥י וְהַפְּרִזִּ֖י בְּיָדָ֑ם וַיַּכּ֣וּם בְּבֶ֔זֶק עֲשֶׂ֥רֶת אֲלָפִ֖ים אִֽישׁ׃

records.literal_gloss: And went up Judah, and gave Yahweh the Canaanite[s] and the Perizzite[s] into their hand, and they struck them at Bezek, ten thousand man.

en.L: And Judah went up, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand, and they struck them at Bezek, 10,000 men.
en.B: When Judah went up, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} handed the Canaanites and the Perizzites over to them, and they defeated 10,000 men at Bezek.
en.R: So Judah attacked, and {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} let them defeat the Canaanites and the Perizzites. At the town of Bezek they defeated 10,000 of their men.

sw.L: Naye Yuda akapanda, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawatia Wakanaani na Waperizi mkononi mwao, nao wakawapiga huko Bezeki, watu elfu kumi.
sw.B: Yuda alipopanda, {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} aliwatia Wakanaani na Waperizi mikononi mwao, nao wakawashinda watu elfu kumi huko Bezeki.
sw.R: Basi watu wa Yuda walishambulia, naye {{divine_name:BWANA|Yahwe}} akawawezesha kuwashinda Wakanaani na Waperizi. Katika mji wa Bezeki waliwashinda watu wao elfu kumi.

es.L: Y subió Judá, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} entregó a los cananeos y a los ferezeos en su mano, y los hirieron en Bezec, diez mil hombres.
es.B: Cuando Judá subió, {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les entregó a los cananeos y a los ferezeos, y derrotaron a diez mil hombres en Bezec.
es.R: Entonces Judá atacó, y {{divine_name:el SEÑOR|Yahvé}} les dio la victoria sobre los cananeos y los ferezeos. En la ciudad de Bezec derrotaron a diez mil de sus hombres.

fr.L: Et Juda monta, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} livra les Cananéens et les Phéréziens dans leur main, et ils les frappèrent à Bézeq, dix mille hommes.
fr.B: Juda monta, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui livra les Cananéens et les Phéréziens ; ils battirent dix mille hommes à Bézeq.
fr.R: La tribu de Juda a donc attaqué, et {{divine_name:le SEIGNEUR|Yahvé}} lui a donné la victoire sur les Cananéens et les Phéréziens. Près de la ville de Bézeq, ses hommes ont battu dix mille de leurs soldats.

vi.L: Và Giu-đa đi lên, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} phó người Ca-na-an và người Phê-rê-sít vào tay họ; và họ đánh giết chúng tại Bê-xéc, mười nghìn người.
vi.B: Khi Giu-đa đi lên, {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} giao người Ca-na-an và người Phê-rê-sít cho họ, và họ đánh bại mười nghìn người tại Bê-xéc.
vi.R: Vậy quân Giu-đa tấn công, và {{divine_name:CHÚA|Gia-vê}} cho họ thắng người Ca-na-an và người Phê-rê-sít. Tại thành Bê-xéc, họ đánh bại mười nghìn người của quân địch.

ko.L: 그리고 유다가 올라갔고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 가나안 사람들과 브리스 사람들을 그들의 손에 주셨다. 그들이 베섹에서 그들을 쳤는데, 만 명이었다.
ko.B: 유다가 올라가자 {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서 가나안 사람들과 브리스 사람들을 그들에게 넘겨주셨다. 그들은 베섹에서 만 명을 쳐부수었다.
ko.R: 그래서 유다 사람들이 공격했고, {{divine_name:주|야훼}}께서는 그들이 가나안 사람들과 브리스 사람들을 이기게 하셨다. 그들은 베섹 성읍에서 적군 만 명을 무찔렀다.

pt.L: E Judá subiu, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} entregou os cananeus e os ferezeus na mão deles, e os feriram em Bezeque: dez mil homens.
pt.B: Quando Judá subiu, {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} entregou nas mãos deles os cananeus e os ferezeus, e eles derrotaram dez mil homens em Bezeque.
pt.R: Então Judá atacou, e {{divine_name:o SENHOR|Javé}} fez com que eles vencessem os cananeus e os ferezeus. Na cidade de Bezeque, derrotaram dez mil homens deles.

decisions.choice: the Perizzites; Bezek: a people of the land and a town whose site is uncertain
decisions.reason: The Perizzites are named beside the Canaanites as people of the land from Abraham's time (Genesis 13:7; 34:30). Bezek is not known for certain. A Bezek in 1 Samuel 11:8 lay farther north, near the Jordan, and may or may not be the same place.

decisions.choice: ten thousand: the word for "thousand" may also name a unit of fighting men
decisions.reason: As noted at Numbers 1, the word for "thousand" can also be used of a military or clan unit, which would give a smaller number of men.

decisions.choice: the LORD gave them into their hand: the LORD gave Judah the victory
decisions.reason: The words fulfil the promise of verse 2. The battle is told as the LORD's gift before it is told as Judah's deed.

decisions.choice: the town of
decisions.reason: Readable adds "the town of" before Bezek so the reader knows it is a place.

decisions.choice: the peoples and places of this chapter in their usual Spanish forms: "los ferezeos", "Bezec", "Adoni-bezec", "Quiriat-arbá", "Sesai", "Ahimán", "Talmai", "Debir", "Quiriat-séfer", "Acsa", "Otoniel hijo de Quenaz", "el Néguev", "la Sefelá", "Horma", "Ascalón", "Ecrón", "los jebuseos", "Betel", "Luz", "Bet-seán", "Taanac", "Meguido", "Quitrón", "Naalal", "Aco", "Aczib", "Afec", "Bet-semes", "Bet-anat", "Ajalón", "Saalbim", "Acrabim"
alternatives: closer transcriptions of the Hebrew ("Perizitas", "Qiryat Arba")
decisions.reason: For the whole of Judges: names follow the forms long used in Spanish Bibles, with Spanish accents, and the forms already used in the Pentateuch ("los ferezeos", "Quiriat-arbá", "Horma", "el Néguev", "la Sefelá"). Readable adds "la ciudad de" only where the English Readable says "the town of".

decisions.choice: "les Phéréziens", "Bézeq", and the other names of the chapter in their French form ("Adoni-Bézeq", "Kiryath-Arba", "Kiryath-Sépher", "Aksa", "Otniel", "Horma", "Beth-Shéan", "Meguiddo", "Guézer")
decisions.reason: For Judges 1-10: names follow the forms already used in the French Pentateuch where there is one ("les Phéréziens", "les Jébusiens", "les Kéniens", "Horma", "Anaq") and the terms note for Joshua, Judges and Ruth ("Otniel", "Éhoud", "Débora", "Yaël", "Gédéon", "Abimélek"); other names transcribe the Hebrew with French accents, writing "q" for qof (Bézeq) and "sh" for shin (Beth-Shéan).

decisions.choice: os ferezeus; Bezeque; dez mil
decisions.reason: "Os ferezeus" is the form Genesis 13:7 and Joshua use in Portuguese. "Bezeque" takes the Brazilian ending for the Hebrew final k, as "Melquisedeque" and "Adoni-Zedeque" do. A round number is written in words in running text (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 5).
